title: Even or Odd
description: Learn to determine if numbers are even or odd using the modulo operator, handle edge cases, and work with arrays of numbers.

steps.title: Check if a number is even
steps.description: Write an `isEven` function that returns `true` if a number is even and `false` otherwise. Use the modulo operator (`%`).
hints: A number is even if number % 2 === 0
The function should return a boolean: true or false

verification.successMessage: The isEven function correctly identifies even and odd numbers!
verification.failureMessage: isEven(4) should return true, isEven(7) should return false.

steps.title: Return 'even' or 'odd' as a string
steps.description: Create an `evenOrOdd` function that returns the string `"even"` or `"odd"` instead of a boolean.
hints: Use an if/else statement to return different strings

verification.successMessage: Now your function returns helpful strings!
verification.failureMessage: evenOrOdd(4) should return 'even', evenOrOdd(7) should return 'odd'.

steps.title: Handle edge cases
steps.description: Extend `evenOrOdd` to handle edge cases: zero (even), negative numbers, and decimals (not integers).
hints: Negative numbers work with % too: -3 % 2 === -1, check if === 0 or !== 0
Use Number.isInteger() to check if a number has decimals
Return "not an integer" for decimal numbers

verification.successMessage: Your function handles all edge cases!
verification.failureMessage: Make sure 0 returns 'even', -3 returns 'odd', and 2.5 returns 'not an integer'.

steps.title: Filter an array
steps.description: Use the `isEven` function with JavaScript's `.filter()` method to get only even numbers from an array.
hints: Arrays have a .filter() method that takes a function
Pass isEven as the callback: numbers.filter(isEven)
The result is a new array with only even numbers

steps.title: Count evens and odds
steps.description: Write a `countEvensOdds` function that takes an array and returns an object with counts of even and odd numbers.
hints: Loop through the array and check each number
Keep two counters: one for evens, one for odds
Return an object like { evens: 3, odds: 4 }

verification.successMessage: You built a counting function that works with real data!
verification.failureMessage: For [1,2,3,4,5,6], there should be 3 evens and 3 odds.
